pr_body:
- git: Return body from list of commits
    This allow to use body of every commits between two ref.

- pr: Add flag fillverbose
    This is used to fill the body of PR with all commits msg + body


Motivation: Usually I have lot of information within the body of commit msg, as you know many project had this situation, i.e. kernel. With this flag we can keep compatibility to previous flags but add a special behaviour if a developer put lot of effort in writing good commits.
(This pr is opened with this flag :) )


Bonus: Another thing that I would love to see is the same feature but when a PR is already opened, in this way we can backfill description of PR with the same content of commits. 

Fixes: #8445

issue_context.title: Open a PR with all commits title + body as PR description
issue_context.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

Often, when individuals compose detailed commit messages along with informative bodies, it can be cumbersome to manually copy and paste this information into a GitHub pull request description. Fortunately, using a straightforward command, it is possible to automatically generate a comprehensive list of commits, complete with titles and bodies. This simplifies the process of creating a high-quality pull request description effortlessly.

### Proposed solution

I propose a new flag to this in order to keep the current behavior untouched `gh pr create --fillverbose`

@guerinoni : thank you for opening up this enhancement idea! 🤗 

**Could you share an example of what this would look like?**  I'm not sure if you have an arbitrary repository with commits that you have been using for development purposes, but it would help the maintainers see what the git history and the resulting PR would look like with this proposed change.

Yes, I present you an example from another repository. Let say I have those 2 commits

```
commit 2952f01e84cdbcb46a69be282ce3053226c18a41
Author: Aliaksandr Kalenik <kalenik.aliaksandr@gmail.com>
Date:   Mon Dec 11 16:47:40 2023 +0100

    LibWeb: Add pair of methods to apply/reset scroll offset of paintable

    Separate scroll application from before_children_paint and
    after_children_paint.

commit 8eacb81ebaf229e947b22beaf581e1860e48076e
Author: Andreas Kling <kling@serenityos.org>
Date:   Mon Dec 11 16:50:04 2023 +0100

    LibJS: Skip redundant marking of Shape property table keys

    All the keys in a property table are guaranteed to be marked via
    Shape::m_property_key in each step of the transition chain that leads
    up to the Shape.
```

Right now if I do `gh pr create` the GH PR description will be
```
- LibWeb: Add pair of methods to apply/reset scroll offset of paintable
- LibJS: Skip redundant marking of Shape property table keys
```
This is good, but why should I re-write all details that I already put as git msg body?
Basically because if you do rebae and merge you will keep all commits, and this is good to check offline from git command line.

With my changes, already in PR linked the output would be `gh pr create --autofillverbose`
```
- LibWeb: Add pair of methods to apply/reset scroll offset of paintable
   Separate scroll application from before_children_paint and
   after_children_paint.
- LibJS: Skip redundant marking of Shape property table keys
   All the keys in a property table are guaranteed to be marked via
   Shape::m_property_key in each step of the transition chain that leads
   up to the Shape.
```

At least it is more complete, maybe you want summarize all thing in a bunch of words, but as default behavior without doing it manually it is a good output :)
